owner_authorization.source: explicit Owner instruction in the active session

baseline_note: Source worktree J5A was cumulative and did not descend from the current main; this J5B worktree starts from its final commit without rewriting that lineage.

diagnosis.validator_preflight_scope: per mesh validation call; aggregate of reduced stiffness and mass sparse terms and the requested eigenpairs for that mesh
diagnosis.allow_inconclusive_behavior: keeps computed frequencies and modes available and reports float residual and mass-orthogonality diagnostics; it does not certify the budget-limited modal residual

comparison_reference.type: independent analytical Kirchhoff thin-plate Navier solution

formulation_background.title: Influence of Rotatory Inertia and Shear on Flexural Motions of Isotropic, Elastic Plates
formulation_background.author: R. D. Mindlin

hypotheses: flat homogeneous isotropic linearly elastic square plate
small-amplitude free vibration with transverse displacement zero on all edges
Kirchhoff thin-plate continuum; no transverse-shear deformation or rotary inertia
comparison_reference.compatibility_limit: The QF model uses Reissner-Mindlin MITC4 with shear_factor=5/6 and consistent rotary mass. At t/a=0.01 Navier is a thin-plate reference, not an exact discrete or Mindlin solution; theory and discretization effects remain combined.

model.geometry: 1.0 m x 1.0 m square flat mid-surface; thickness 0.01 m; normal +Z
model.material: E=70 GPa, nu=0.3, density=2700 kg/m^3, SI, isotropic shell
model.supports: UZ=0 on all four perimeter edges; rotations free; UX=UY=0 at node 0 and UY=0 at node n*(n+1) to remove in-plane rigid modes
model.analysis: linear free vibration; six lowest generalized modes; dense eigh; consistent mass with translational and tangential rotary inertia; no preload or damping
model.validation_policy: allow_inconclusive; no validator threshold or algorithm is changed

resource_assessment: Retains the J5A envelope; five small dense mesh solves are bounded to one process/thread. Before freezing J5B, the observed environment had approximately 43 GiB free disk, 60 GiB available RAM, Python 3.13.1, NumPy 2.2.6, SciPy 1.15.2, and Matplotlib 3.10.3.

indicators_and_existing_route_checks.frequency: report first four computed candidate frequencies and absolute relative errors to the same four Navier references at every mesh
indicators_and_existing_route_checks.mode_shape: unweighted nodal MAC for modes 11 and 22; minimum principal-angle squared (subspace MAC) for repeated 12/21 pair
indicators_and_existing_route_checks.solver_quality: report maximum relative residual and mass-orthogonality diagnostics at every mesh; identify their floating diagnostic status
indicators_and_existing_route_checks.mesh_trend: report whether first frequency error improves from coarsest to finest; do not fit a convergence order

route_thresholds.source: unchanged constants in Mitc4SimplySupportedPlateStudy, inherited from J5A

indicators_and_existing_route_checks.campaign_status_rule: if any mesh validation is INCONCLUSIVE, campaign status remains INCONCLUSIVE regardless of frequency, MAC, residual, or orthogonality diagnostics; only PASS_CERTIFIED at every mesh and all inherited route checks can yield PASS

attempts.retry_policy: one J5B campaign attempt; any timeout or diagnostic failure consumes it

artifacts: runner preflight, stdout/stderr, run record, and distinct durable J5B attempt ledger
atomic JSON and NPZ checkpoint per mesh with source/input provenance, phase, candidate vectors, frequencies, diagnostics, and exact validation state when available
summary.json, site_data.json, frequency CSV, and finest-mesh candidate modes
mesh/support, frequency comparison, and four-mode figures with visual normalization stated
README with interpretation, limitations, and reproducibility route
limitations: Any INCONCLUSIVE validation remains an exploratory candidate, not a certified modal result.
J5A did not retain serialized frequencies or modes; its PYTEST_FAILED status remains unchanged.
Navier is Kirchhoff thin-plate theory; MITC4 is Reissner-Mindlin and includes shear correction and rotary inertia.
The repeated (1,2)/(2,1) eigenspace is non-unique; individual candidate vectors can rotate or swap.
Visual mode amplitudes are normalized and scaled and do not represent a forced-response displacement.
This run does not qualify the modal route or the solver in general.

execution_environment.budget_semantics: wall timeout and captured-output caps are enforced by the development runner; RSS, process count, temporary/archive size, and free-disk readings are sampled soft observations, not OS quotas
